result:
All clean — `SPEC.md` and `spec-assets/` untouched, `ios/` isn't tracked. The build succeeds end to end. Summary of what was implemented for Phase 3 (Transcribe/Speech):

- **`modules/expo-speech-recognition/`** — new local Expo module (Swift, mirrors `expo-health`'s structure) wrapping `SFSpeechRecognizer`: authorization status/request, and a `transcribeSample()` async function that runs `SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest` against the bundled file with partial results, streaming them via an `onPartialTranscript` event and resolving with the final transcript.
- **`plugins/withSampleAudio.ts`** — a config plugin that copies `spec-assets/sample.wav` into the generated iOS project and wires it into the app target's Copy Bundle Resources during `expo prebuild`, so it's loaded via `Bundle.main` at runtime (no JS-side asset streaming).
- **`app.json`** — added `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` and registered the plugin.
- **`screens/TranscribeScreen.tsx`** — wired to the new module: status line reflects/refreshes authorization on focus, `Request Access` requests it, `Transcribe Sample` (enabled only when granted and idle) streams live partial text into the transcript area, then shows the final transcript plus `Completed in N.N s`; errors surface in the status line and re-enable the button.
- Added `@expo/config-plugins` and `@types/node` as devDependencies for the plugin, and `"types": ["node"]` to `tsconfig.json`.

One thing worth knowing: the `xcode` library's `addResourceFile` has a bug where it always looks for a group literally named "Resources" (unrelated to the target group) and crashes if none exists — the plugin works around it by creating a harmless detached placeholder group.
